subject: Nyx-8B elevated timeouts — impact notice and follow-up
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-22 09:12 AM -0700
Subject: Alert: Nyx-8B elevated 5xx/timeouts (observed at 08:55 PDT)

Team —

Our monitoring detected an uptick in 5xx and client timeouts for model variant Nyx-8B serving in us-west-2 beginning ~08:45 PDT. Error rate has climbed from baseline ~0.3% to ~6% over the last 20 minutes for a subset of customer traffic routed to the tiled batchers. Key observations: 

- Increased RPC timeouts to the frontend (~30–120s ramps)
- Backend logs show intermittent kernel OOM/evict cycles on two GPU nodes (node-az2-gpu-11/12)
- Autoscaler attempted to provision burst capacity but experienced provisioning delays (~6m)

I've attached a short log extract (nyx8b-error-sample-logs.txt). I'm escalating since this is customer-facing and affecting sustained requests for a few enterprise customers (notably MarketLytics).

Immediate asks:
- Connor/Marissa: please coordinate a customer-facing note if this persists beyond 30m.
- Grace/Dylan: ops runbook ownership to check node health, kernel retries, and fallback policy enforcement.

Ben

--
Ben Carter
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com

From: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>
To: Elena Soto <elena@marketlytics.com>
Cc: MarketLytics Platform <platform-support@marketlytics.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-22 09:43 AM -07:00
Subject: Re: Nyx-8B elevated 5xx/timeouts — we're investigating

Hi Elena —

Thanks for the quick flag. Apologies for the disruption — we see elevated 5xx/timeouts on some Nyx-8B serving nodes in us-west-2 that are impacting a small slice of MarketLytics traffic. Our ops engineers are investigating kernel-level evictions and autoscaler delays; we have a mitigation in progress (routing traffic to warm fallback pools) and expect a customer-facing update within 60 minutes.

What we're doing now:
- Redirecting new requests from affected pools to fallback Nyx-8B instances with identical model config.
- Restarting two affected GPU nodes and validating KV cache warm-up.
- Capturing request samples for post-incident analysis.

Could you confirm whether any MarketLytics workflows are extremely latency-sensitive right now (batch inference vs low-latency feature)? That will help prioritize routing policies.

Apologies again — I'll follow up ASAP with status.

Regards,
Connor O'Brien
Account Executive — Strategic Accounts, Redwood Inference
connor.obrien@redwood.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>

Date: 2027-04-22 11:05 AM -07:00
Subject: RE: Nyx-8B elevated 5xx/timeouts — update and temporary fix applied

Connor / Ben / Grace —

Quick operational update: we confirmed kernel OOM churn on az2-gpu-11/12 caused local worker evictions; autoscaler delays were due to transient image-pull timeouts on the new burst hosts (registry rate-limiting causing ~4–7m lag).

Actions completed at 10:58 PDT:
- We rerouted MarketLytics low-latency traffic to prioritized warm pools (nyx8b-warm-priority-1/2) that maintain KV cache warmness and are pinned to lower-density hosts. 
- Replaced az2-gpu-11/12 and rebalanced batchers.
- Applied a short-term registry retry tuning to reduce image-pull retries and prevent further provisioning stalls.

Impact now: error rate for MarketLytics low-latency path down to ~0.7% (from ~8%). Overall Nyx-8B fleet error rate trending down but still slightly elevated (~1.5%). We're keeping prioritized lanes for ML now until 14:00 PDT as a precaution.

Connor — please share a brief note to Elena letting them know prioritized lanes are live and the ETA for full fleet recovery. I'll follow up with a draft postmortem and recommended long-term fixes (registry backoff, node-level guardrails, and proactive warm provisioning windows).

Marissa

--
Marissa Cole
Site Reliability Lead, Redwood Inference

From: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-23 04:40 PM -07:00
Subject: Nyx-8B incident: postmortem summary and next steps (action required)

Elena / MarketLytics team —

Thank you for your patience while we completed the initial investigation. Attached is a concise postmortem draft (postmortem-draft-v1.pdf) summarizing root cause, impact, and our planned fixes. Key takeaways: 

Root cause
- Two GPU hosts (az2-gpu-11/12) experienced repeated kernel-level memory reclaim that triggered worker process evictions. This was correlated with a new background job that increased KV cache churn on those hosts. 
- Autoscaler provisioning attempts were delayed due to registry image-pull rate-limiting (external container registry) which introduced 4–7m cold-start windows.

Customer impact
- MarketLytics experienced ~8% failures on a low-latency scoring path between 08:45–11:00 PDT on Apr 22. We temporarily pinned low-latency requests to warm priority lanes. No data loss observed.

Immediate remediation completed
- Replaced the two faulty GPU hosts and rebalanced workload.
- Applied temporary registry retry/backoff tuning to mitigate image-pull stalls.
- Provisioned warm-priority lanes for MarketLytics until 14:00 PDT; extended to 18:00 PDT at your request.

Planned long-term fixes (timeline)
- Registry backoff and exponential retry improvements (engineering change) — targeted rollout by 2027-05-10.
- Per-host KV cache guardrails and memory throttling to prevent cross-job churn — design review week of 2027-04-26.
- Improved autoscaler telemetry and pre-warm windows for enterprise-tier customers — beta rollout 2027-06.

Action required/asks from MarketLytics
- Confirm whether you want priority lanes kept until 2027-04-30 (we can extend but will need formal approval).
- Share any cropped request logs for 10:40–11:00 PDT if you want us to correlate against our traces (we've already captured server-side samples).

We regret the disruption and will incorporate your feedback into the final postmortem. Please let me know if you'd like a quick 30-minute sync to walk through the findings.

Thanks,
Grace O'Connor
Director, Platform Reliability, Redwood Inference
grace.oconnor@redwood.com
